items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: I had an uncle, Tom, who also loved classical music.

ctx.x: No. No I was just — it was music, they loved music and they played music in the house fairly regularly. I mean one of the big things that I always recalled was on Sunday nights that I remember, as best I remember it, there was a thing called the Bell Telephone Hour I believe. And if I’m not mistaken I think it was the New York Philharmonic or something like that that played. It was a New York symphony orchestra. And my grandmother and my mom, they liked Mario Lanza, the Great Caruso, things like that. They liked…

laying on a little blanket in a diaper you know. But we listened to that music, and I had an uncle, Tom, who also loved classical music. So we’d gather around in the living room and listen to this thing every Sunday night. And I just remember laying there and listening. But the first one that hit me like a bong in the head was when they did “Peter and the Wolf.” I was probably maybe about two or two and a half years old when I heard that. And a bassoon could be a duck? I thought wow that is the hippest thing in…

I had an experience like that at Boy Scout camp with a visiting troop and some song they did with rhythms that I’d never heard before. And I was wondering if you’ve ever had a student who could play technically really well but just seemed devoid of what you’re describing, that the music had no depth or emotion behind it.
